summary.text: Lisa McClain is the Republican incumbent, seeking a fourth term and serving as chair of the House Republican Conference. A Michigan business owner and nonprofit founder before Congress, she was first elected in 2020 and moved into party leadership in 2023. According to her official biography, she works on issues including agriculture, financial services, national defense, immigration, health care and veterans affairs.

paragraphs.text: Born April 7, 1966, in Stockbridge, Michigan, where she was raised and graduated from high school in 1984, according to Wikipedia.
Attended Lansing Community College and earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Northwood University.
According to her official biography, spent more than 30 years building and growing a business before entering Congress. She also founded and served as president of North End Support Team.

Won the 2020 Republican primary for Michigan's open 10th District over Shane Hernandez and Doug Slocum, then defeated Kimberly Bizon (D) in the general election; the district was renumbered the 9th after redistricting, and she won re-election in 2022 and 2024.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee, according to her official biography.
Served as Secretary of the House Republican Conference in the 118th Congress and was elected chair of the Conference for the 119th Congress.
Lives in Romeo, Michigan, with her husband, Mike, and their four children, according to her official biography.
